value_and_effort.method: Before forecasting, obtain observed donor intent and an authorized need/capacity budget; separate pledges, cleared receipts and restricted funds. Reconcile gross receipts to actual fee/refund/chargeback/host/bank/FX deductions and settlement, then deduct required reserves or restrictions from spendable cash. A deduction already reflected in settlement is never subtracted twice.
value_and_effort.payer_vs_recipient: S3's payer charges do not by themselves establish the recipient's net proceeds. Confirm the transaction's actual fee bearer and base; do not promise 100% of gross donations.
value_and_effort.avoided_cost_rule: This is a cash channel. Avoided cost is a separate measured counterfactual for necessary expenditure displaced by usable support, never an additional copy of the same receipt.
value_and_effort.effort_method: Measure the approved profile/terms/identity work, monthly transaction and reconciliation volume, acknowledgment/report effort, exceptions and exit work. Unknown demand or hours stay null; no arbitrary conversion to money or award probability.
value_and_effort.current_conclusion: No defensible amount or numeric score yet. A useful channel design is not a budget, an award or income.

operating_assessment.project_control: Review the exact proposed use and counterparty under the accepted neutrality proposal before any commitment. No ranking, evaluator, source-admission, roadmap, release, security exception or exclusive data right is exchanged for support. Apply actual conflict/recusal and replacement-funding controls; repository access creates no signing authority.

Prepare an account-specific gross-to-net worksheet, fee bearer/base, settlement currency, reserves, refund procedure and private tax review. Keep the observed withholding conflict open. No deduction, tax form, tax threshold, universal payout day or net receipt is promised. Use the actual selected payment role to resolve the S6/S10/S11 instrument and support-contact differences; do not apply Connected Account fees or obligations universally.

No actual binding sponsor report or renewal date is known. Proposed monthly control: reconcile obligations, sponsor transactions, bank/host statements, refunds and restrictions; publish only an approved aggregate progress account. Do not assume a retired tier cancels existing obligations. Recheck current agreements on renewal/change and before adding benefits.

Use neutral, separately consented acknowledgment of actual support. Review profile assets and the actual publicity/content permissions. Do not imply endorsement, GitHub partnership or charitable qualification. Publish reproducible project results under their existing rights; unpublished terms and private donor data require their own authorized handling. Record the exact proposed public Content and its rights under S9; the individual AI Input/Output control is not a substitute for that publication decision.

Keep identity, addresses, tax forms, bank details, authentication material, private agreements and nonpublic donor data out of Git/issues. Verify actual platform/processor/host roles, access, retention and consent before collection. A public profile or ledger must be reviewed for intended visibility; generic privacy rights are not a guaranteed complete erasure or migration. Separate proposed public Content, AI Inputs/Outputs and private administration. Record applicable controller/processor roles, agreement and settings without inferring that every private datum is used for training or that repository exclusion prevents all processing.

Prepare the actual host/processor exit and remaining-balance plan, permissible export, retention, restricted-fund disposition and sponsor communication. Do not assume recurring payment instructions or donor consent can be transferred. Preserve project source and evaluation independence if support stops. Identify which actual payment/portal/host contract governs access, support and termination before promising an export or account disconnection.

A donation channel has no compute-credit overage allowance. Downstream service bills, benefit fulfillment, refunds and professional work remain separately bounded commitments. If support falls short, pause proposed spending under the actual controls; there is no automatic paid fallback or personal reimbursement.

sources.title: Organization setup
sources.scope: Complete public organization setup guidance; no authenticated organization form or account inspected.
sources.finding: An organization owner applies for an open-source contributor legally operating in a supported region. The guide describes a waitlist/invitation, contact/profile, payout/tax information, 2FA and approval. Choose a bank account or supported fiscal host during signup; later host changes go through Support. The setter's residence must match the supported bank region. Optional tiers: ten monthly and ten one-time, USD, up to USD 12,000 per month. Published tier prices cannot be edited for existing subscribers. Approval publishes the profile. These platform capabilities are not a verified mandate, account, invitation or safe tier design for PYA.
sources.version_limit: Undated live guide; its organization tax-form shortcut must not replace the dedicated tax guidance or the actual recipient's requirements.

sources.title: Fiscal-host payout compatibility
sources.finding: The published supported list names Hack Club, NumFOCUS, Open Collective Europe, Open Source Collective, Python Software Foundation, Radiant Earth and Software in the Public Interest. Signup requests the selected host and the project's profile URL to confirm its existing relationship. SPI and OSC therefore have a documented integration. SFC is not listed in this inspected version; its specific route needs provider confirmation. Listing establishes neither host admission nor a PYA relationship.

sources.title: Program scope, payer fees and historical matching
sources.scope: Complete public program overview, supported-region list and matching section.
sources.finding: The program supports financial contributions to eligible open-source work. Personal-account sponsorships have no GitHub fee. Organization-funded sponsorships can incur up to 6%: 3% service and 3% card processing; invoiced billing can remove the card portion. This distinction concerns the payer, not whether the recipient is an organization. The old Matching Fund application cutoff was January 1, 2020. Organizations cannot receive matching and organization-funded payments are not match eligible. No matching amount is available to this assessment.

sources.title: Tax information
sources.scope: Complete public tax guide; no tax form, identity data or actual tax position reviewed.
sources.finding: The dedicated guide distinguishes US W-9 from non-US W-8 routes and individual from company recipients, using Stripe collection. Tax responsibility and treatment are recipient specific. The guide's categorical no-withholding statement differs from S6's reservation of required withholding. Its stated reporting threshold is not adopted as a verified 2026 legal threshold. No form, tax classification, deduction or zero-withholding conclusion is selected for PYA.

sources.title: Payout management
sources.scope: Complete public payout guide; no dashboard, payout statement or bank receipt inspected.
sources.finding: The dashboard distinguishes past from estimated payouts; Stripe payout records can be exported as PDFs. Host changes use Support. Timing is referred to the Additional Terms.

sources.title: Sponsors Additional Terms
sources.scope: Public recipient, sponsor and general terms, including sections 3-5 and general A-H. The two public instruments linked by 3.8 were separately read as S10-S11; the actual account, route, country-specific Services Agreement and any host/portal agreement remain unverified.
sources.finding: Truthful identity, lawful activity, content rights and signing authority are required; fraud and self-dealing are restricted. Stripe controls custody and payment processing. Recipient payments can be reduced or held for fees, taxes, refunds, chargebacks or breaches. Timing differs by route, first payment, threshold, country and termination; no universal payout date is promised. Recipients specify refund terms. Stripe agreements and information sharing depend on account country. Recipient termination can occur with or without cause or notice; payer invoicing has separate renewal rules. Publicity, confidentiality, assignment restrictions and change notices also apply. Actual payment, privacy, liability and exit terms require review before commitment.

sources.title: General Privacy Statement
sources.scope: Scoped read: applicability and controller/processor limits; account/payment/profile data; purposes including model development, affiliate sharing, privacy rights, international transfers and retention. Actual account settings, organization contracts and other processors' policies were not qualified.
sources.finding: GitHub describes personal-data processing for service improvement, including model training, and affiliate sharing including Microsoft. Organization-provided accounts and contractual controller/processor arrangements have different stated scope. Public visibility, jurisdiction-dependent rights and legal retention limits remain relevant. This does not establish training on every private donor/payment datum or complete erasure/portability. S9 separately assesses submitted Content and AI Input/Output rights.

sources.title: Public Sponsors entry point
sources.scope: Complete public landing page read after redirect; sign-in and Get sponsored links observed. No authenticated application was opened or submitted.
sources.finding: The existing record's application URL redirects to a public overview with a Get sponsored entry. Marketing examples and launch-in-minutes language do not establish PYA approval, intake completion, donor demand or guaranteed proceeds.

sources.title: GitHub Terms of Service: content and AI data-use scope
sources.scope: Direct public read of definitions; D.3-D.8, E and J.1-J.3, with surrounding terms context. Actual Customer/volume agreements and account settings remain unverified.
sources.finding: D.4-D.8 license GitHub/affiliate use of submitted Content, expressly including AI training, and describe public access, repository licenses and attribution limits. J.3 separately addresses individual AI Inputs/Outputs: its prospective opt-out does not override D.4-D.8. Customer/volume arrangements have their own stated scope. E distinguishes private-repository access and content supplied as AI Input. Publishing a profile or repository record therefore needs a content-rights review; withholding a private record from Git does not disable other provider processing.

sources.title: Stripe Recipient Notice
sources.scope: Complete public Recipient Info text, its displayed update date and default English entry. The author's page displayed United States (English); that presentation does not establish PYA's country or actual payout route.
sources.finding: The current target of Sponsors 3.8's recipient link is titled Recipient Notice. It describes transfers on a Payouts User's instructions, possible separate information-portal terms and payment-status questions directed to that user unless instructed otherwise. In this recipient role it offers no Stripe services and says the Services Agreement does not apply. A possible separate agreement with the Payouts User remains distinct; support alone creates no Stripe contract.

sources.title: Stripe Connected Account Agreement
sources.scope: Complete public agreement text, sections 1-8 and displayed modified date. The default English page does not identify PYA's Stripe Account Country or applicable Services Agreement.
sources.finding: For an enrolled Connected Account, this agreement incorporates its account-country Services Agreement. It addresses platform-directed activity and access, data/consent responsibilities, fees and termination; ending it need not end the Services Agreement. Section 7 excludes specified transfers outside Stripe Payments Services and directs those status questions to the platform. These provisions cannot be assumed to govern every Sponsors recipient payout.
